ambiguities.aspect: Initial/reset value of q (no reset port specified)
readings: q has no defined reset; its value is unknown/uninitialized (X in simulation) until the first rising clock edge loads d, so the first-cycle output is indeterminate
An implicit power-on/async reset to 8'h00 is assumed (some tools/implementations infer one), so q reads 8'h00 until d is loaded

ambiguities.aspect: Bit ordering between d and q
readings: Identity mapping: q[i] is the flip-flop driven by d[i] for i=0..7, so q tracks d directly
Reversed mapping: q[7-i] is driven by d[i] (bit-endianness swap), so q equals the bit-reversed value of d

ambiguities.aspect: Output latency / number of register stages on q
readings: q is the direct output of the 8 D flip-flops: q changes one rising edge after d is captured (1-cycle latency)
The 8 DFFs form a pipeline whose output is further registered/conditioned so q appears two edges after d, or is additionally gated by clock enable logic
